title: Diamond Framework: Reputation-Weighted Validator Selection via Verifiable Non-Transferable Reputation
description: Paper and repository for the Diamond Framework, v0.2.2. Includes: the paper source and PDF (43 pp, sha256 5651a2f3...), a 38-script verification suite with byte-identical reruns, a falsification log (22 entries), an Avalanche Fuji phase-1 deployment with on-chain wiring verified, an 11-file anchor root, and OpenTimestamps receipts (the receipt over root 5ff84501 is Bitcoin-attested in blocks 972674, 972682 and 972749). v0.2.2 is a text release: it removes the statements that v0.2.1 could only correct in an errata sheet. Section 6 now describes the validator-bound statement that M4d delivers (Poseidon leaf with the validator address as a public input); the verification cost is the measured cold path, 286,144 gas (781 gwei break-even, 31x margin at 25 gwei) instead of the ~206k composition with an inlined key; the collusion detector declares W as an external input (D-7) and the on-chain alert as a non-sanction; the financial floor is stated as a minimum admission cost, not a guarantee; and the README lists the five roles v1 trusts. Earlier releases: v0.2.1 corrected the ZK paper-code mismatch (measured V3/Groth16 circuit, 94,438 constraints; recursion deferred); v0.1.0 was the first deposit. Verification: the offline Foundry and Rust suites plus the 38-script evidence harness, 11/11 audit gate. The anchor root covers eleven files. On the Fuji testnet a Groth16 verifier built from the repository's committed development key is deployed and announced through the registry's two-day guardian rotation: it carries no ceremony, records no certified admission, and the ceremony-key verifier, the recursive option and Teleporter cross-subnet latency remain declared deferred. The repository code is MIT; the manuscript and the frozen PDF are CC BY 4.0.
